options.text: The process by which cells divide
The process by which cells die
The process by which a cell becomes specialised for a particular function
The process by which cells produce energy

questions.explanation: Cell differentiation is the process by which a cell develops specialised structures and functions, becoming adapted for a particular role in the organism.

questions.stem: Why do red blood cells have a biconcave disc shape?

options.text: To carry nerve impulses more quickly
To allow them to divide more easily
To increase surface area for oxygen absorption

questions.explanation: The biconcave disc shape of red blood cells increases their surface area to volume ratio, allowing more efficient absorption and release of oxygen.

questions.stem: Which specialised cell has many mitochondria to provide energy for movement?
questions.explanation: Sperm cells have many mitochondria arranged in the middle section to provide the energy needed to power the tail for swimming towards the egg.

questions.stem: What is the main adaptation of root hair cells?

options.text: They have a thick cell wall for support
They lack a nucleus to carry more oxygen
They have a long extension to increase surface area for water absorption

questions.explanation: Root hair cells have a long, thin extension (the root hair) that greatly increases the surface area available for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil.

questions.stem: Why do nerve cells (neurones) have a long axon?

options.text: To carry electrical impulses over long distances

questions.explanation: Nerve cells have a long axon that can be up to a metre long, allowing them to transmit electrical impulses rapidly over long distances in the body.

questions.stem: Which cell is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Palisade mesophyll cells are found near the top surface of the leaf and are packed with chloroplasts to maximise the amount of photosynthesis they can carry out.

questions.stem: What is unusual about mature red blood cells?

options.text: They are the largest cells in the body

questions.explanation: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, which provides more space for haemoglobin to carry oxygen. They are also one of the few cell types without a nucleus.
